result.keywords:
Abstract
               Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis often requires both robust imputation of dropout events and accurate cell-type classification. Existing workflows typically address these tasks separately, yet downstream annotation quality can depend strongly on how missing values are handled. In this study, we benchmark a set of imputation-aware single-cell classifiers on diverse scRNA-seq data sets, comparing cluster-level and reference-based strategies under varying dropout rates, class imbalance, and small training cohorts. Results indicate that hybrid methods combining matrix-decomposition imputation with ensemble classification can improve prediction stability, while correlation-based approaches remain competitive when reference labels are noisy. However, no single method consistently detects novel cell populations under all conditions, highlighting the need for adaptive unassigned-label strategies and better integration of denoising with annotation. This work offers practical guidance for selecting methods in scRNA-seq pipelines and suggests future directions for jointly modeling sparsity and cell identity.
result.title: Benchmarking imputation-aware classifiers for single-cell RNA sequencing data sets
